assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: Treat predictable flow and spontaneous access as separate service goals. Preserve walk-in capacity, non-online booking, flexible arrival, and help at the door. Measure waiting, closures, unused slots, turn-aways, workload, and who can actually use each path.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: Agreed. Record current waits, turn-aways, abandoned visits, and closures by time and visitor type before the change. The goal is not to preserve an unmeasured queue. A pilot can test whether reservations reduce those burdens while ensuring that people without advance plans retain a workable route into the exhibition.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: That protects several access modes and limits the penalty for imperfect timing. Test the phone and desk paths under real demand, make the walk-in allocation visible, and avoid releasing all returned capacity through the online channel. Decide how school and community groups fit without allowing block bookings to consume the public allotment.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: Assisted booking can correct a channel barrier if the admission opportunity remains comparable. Publish the size and purpose of the block, review whether it is used, and release unused places. The relevant question is whether people can exercise the same public entitlement, not whether every route has identical mechanics.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: The data use is proportionate to the booking task. Verify deletion, minimize what appears on staff screens, and explain the distinction between a reservation record and anonymous walk-in entry. Keep donor and membership systems technically separate, not merely governed by a promise that the data will not be interesting later.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: Those conditions let the operation adapt without converting every adjustment into failure. Predefine how waits and turn-aways are counted, including people who leave before reaching the desk. The automatic contract end prevents passive continuation, and public weekly results make it harder to redefine success after seeing which channel performs best.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: The proposal is ready as a narrow, observable trial. It compares the booking system with the actual unequal queue, not an idealized open door. Walk-in space remains throughout; phone, desk, and assisted booking reduce channel dependence; privacy is limited; and access failures can change the allocation before the final board review. Execute the counting method as written, especially abandoned visits and walk-in turn-aways, and record any protocol change. The board should see the complete access pattern rather than reservation volume or photographs of orderly galleries.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: You are right; I treated the channels as visitor types. Measure the path used and practical flexibility separately. Offer reliable same-day return times without eliminating immediate entry for people who cannot return. A short voluntary question can reveal the difference, but entry must not become a survey exercise.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: Use a household-sized cap and a separate assisted path for larger groups rather than introducing an account solely to police scarcity. Make cancellation easy, release unconfirmed capacity gradually, and watch whether the confirmation step disproportionately removes people with limited connectivity. Free access can still require fair-use rules, but the enforcement mechanism should not create a larger barrier than the behavior it prevents.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: Do not suppress tourism promotion just to balance the channels. Stagger releases, preserve walk-in and same-day capacity, and publish the same information through libraries, community partners, and the entrance. Review distribution without creating a residency test.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: Recalculate all channel counts using the new safety limit while preserving the agreed proportion unless evidence shows it is unworkable. Returned reservations are not equivalent to dependable walk-in capacity because their timing is uncertain. If crowding creates unsafe queues outside, use same-day timed walk-in tickets and the early adjustment rule rather than quietly reallocating access before observation.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: The final design now responds to visitor behavior rather than forcing people into “planner” and “walk-in” categories. It protects immediate access, offers reliable same-day returns, staggers advance release, and handles larger groups without requiring accounts or residency tests. It also keeps the fire marshal's safety adjustment from silently rewriting the access promise before observation. Preserve the baseline finding that many walk-ins had planned their visit, the booking-page test, confirmation losses, promotion channels, revised occupancy, outside-queue conditions, and every allocation change. The board should see who waited, who returned, who abandoned the visit, and which channel actually worked for whom—not merely whether galleries looked calmer or the reservation system filled its slots.
